2609.13524.title: Rolling Day-Wise Mortality Prediction in Critically Ill Patients With AKI on CRRT Utilizing Machine Pressure Waveforms
2609.13524.paper_summary: Critically ill patients with acute kidney injury (AKI) on continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) face high mortality, yet current risk assessment relies primarily on clinical parameters from electronic health records (EHR) and ignores minute-level circuit pressure waveforms generated by CRRT machines that track the extracorporeal circuit's interaction with the patient. Clinicians therefore cannot see deterioration as it develops. Risk is reassessed only when labs are drawn, while this continuous record is discarded because it is contaminated by shared-device records, non-physiological minutes, and sensor artifacts. To make the stream usable, we aligned machine records to charted therapy intervals to prevent cross-patient leakage, removed priming and downtime minutes, tuned denoising on a synthetic spike-injection benchmark, and masked unobserved intervals rather than imputing them. On this cleaned stream, we define a rolling day-wise task and a transformer-based stacked ensemble that late-fuses a window-reduced sequence transformer with classical models using circuit-instability features and clinical EHR variables. In a leak-safe benchmark on the multi-center CRRTnet cohort (976 patients, 4,585 treatment days), the machine-only model had the lowest standalone prognostic value (AUROC 0.625), followed by the EHR-only model (0.717). Integrating EHR and machine streams reached a one-day mortality AUROC of 0.766. SHAP attribution showed that circuit-instability descriptors raised the machine share of the top 15 combined-model features from 3 to 7 (20.0% to 46.7%), highlighting filter pressure, transmembrane pressure (TMP), and access-to-return difference (ARD). To our knowledge, this is the first patient-level mortality prediction incorporating CRRT machine data, turning a discarded bedside stream into a continuous risk signal.
2609.13524.paper_summary_zh: 重症患者在持續性腎臟替代療法 (CRRT) 中出現急性腎損傷 (AKI) 的死亡率很高，然而目前的風險評估主要依賴電子健康記錄 (EHR) 中的臨床參數，並忽略了由 CRRT 機器生成的、跟蹤體外循環與患者互動的分鐘級電路壓力波形。因此，臨床醫生無法在病情惡化時及時察覺。風險僅在抽取實驗室檢查時重新評估，而這一連續記錄因受共享設備記錄、非生理學分鐘和傳感器伪影的污染而被丟棄。為了使這一數據流可用，我們將機器記錄與標記的治療間隔對齊，以防止跨患者洩漏，移除了啟動和停機分鐘，對合成尖峰注入基準進行了去噪調整，並對未觀察到的間隔進行了遮罩，而不是進行插補。在這一清理後的數據流上，我們定義了一個滾動的日常任務和一個基於Transformer的堆疊集成，該集成將窗口減少的序列Transformer與使用電路不穩定性特徵和臨床 EHR 變量的經典模型進行後期融合。在多中心 CRRTnet 隊列（976 名患者，4,585 天治療）的安全基準測試中，僅使用機器的模型具有最低的單獨預測價值（AUROC 0.625），其次是僅使用 EHR 的模型（0.717）。整合 EHR 和機器數據流達到了每日死亡率 AUROC 0.766。SHAP 歸因顯示，電路不穩定性描述符將前 15 個組合模型特徵中機器的比例從 3 提高到 7（從 20.0% 提高到 46.7%），突出了過濾壓力、跨膜壓力 (TMP) 和進出差異 (ARD)。據我們所知，這是第一個結合 CRRT 機器數據的患者級死亡預測，將被丟棄的床邊數據流轉變為持續的風險信號。
